questions.question:
An athlete runs on a circular track with a diameter of 300 m and completes one round in 50 seconds. If the athlete runs for 2 minutes and 30 seconds, what is the total distance covered from the starting point?

(Use pi = 3.14)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total time = 2 minutes 30 seconds = 150 seconds.

Number of rounds = Total time ÷ Time per round = 150 ÷ 50 = 3 rounds.

Distance of 1 round = π × Diameter = 3.14 × 300 = 942 m.

Total distance = 3 × 942 = 2826 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 2826 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Diameter (d) = 300 m

Time for one round = 50 seconds

Total running time = 2 minutes 30 seconds

Value of π = 3.14

**Formula Used:**

Circumference of circular track = π × d

Total distance = Number of rounds × Circumference

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e075d101a4671d1282201596f22743df453f0eb462148e3c369f9bdb4d10fecf.png] 

⇒ Total running time = (2 × 60) + 30 = 150 seconds

⇒ Circumference (Distance of 1 round) = 3.14 × 300

⇒ Circumference = 942 m

⇒ Number of rounds = 150 / 50

⇒ Number of rounds = 3

⇒ Total Distance = 3 × 942

⇒ Total Distance = 2826 m

**∴ The correct answer is 2826 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Displacement on Circular Path

If an athlete completes an integer number of rounds, the net displacement is 0 as the starting and ending points are the same.

Area of Circular Track

The total area enclosed by the circular track is calculated using Area = πr², where r is the radius (diameter/2).

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. In this case, Speed = 2826 ÷ 150 = 18.84 m/s.</p

questions.question: What does Snell’s Law of refraction state about the relationship between the angle of incidence and the angle of refraction for the given pair of media?

options.text: Both angles are always equal in all media.
The ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence to the sine of the angle of refraction remains constant.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence to the sine of the angle of refraction remains constant**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Snell’s Law of Refraction** is a fundamental principle in **optics** that describes how light bends when passing from one medium to another.
 
• It states that the ratio of the **sine of the angle of incidence** (represented as **sin i**) to the **sine of the angle of refraction** (represented as **sin r**) is a **constant** for a given pair of media and for light of a specific color or **wavelength**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• The mathematical expression for this law is **sin i / sin r = μ** (or **n**), where **μ** is the **Refractive Index** of the second medium relative to the first.
 
• **Snell’s Law** is also known as the **second law of refraction**. It was discovered by the Dutch astronomer and mathematician **Willebrord Snellius** in the year **1621**.
 
• The **angle of incidence** is the angle between the incoming ray and the **normal** (perpendicular) to the interface, while the **angle of refraction** is the angle between the refracted ray and the normal.
 
• This law applies specifically to **monochromatic light**, as different colors of light have different refractive indices in the same medium, a phenomenon known as **dispersion**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Refraction of Light:**
 
 
• **Refraction** is the change in direction of a wave passing from one medium to another caused by its change in speed.
 
• When light travels from a **rarer medium** (like air) to a **denser medium** (like glass or water), it slows down and bends **towards the normal**.
 
• Conversely, when light travels from a **denser medium** to a **rarer medium**, it speeds up and bends **away from the normal**.
 
 
 
• **Refractive Index (n):**
 
 
• The **refractive index** is a dimensionless number that indicates the light-bending ability of a medium.
 
• It is defined as the ratio of the **speed of light in a vacuum** (approximately **3 x 10⁸ m/s**) to the **speed of light in the medium**.
 
• **Absolute Refractive Index** is calculated relative to a vacuum, while **Relative Refractive Index** is calculated between two specific media.
 
 
 
• **Behavior of Other Options:**
 
 
• The statement that "Both angles are always equal" refers to the **Law of Reflection**, not refraction. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The statement "Their difference is always constant" does not correspond to any standard physical law of optics. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The statement "Their sum is always 90°" is only true in the specific case of **Brewster's Law**, where the reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular to each other. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Change in Properties:** During the process of **refraction**, the **velocity** and **wavelength** of light change, but the **frequency** remains **constant**. The frequency is a characteristic of the source of light.
 
• **Normal Incidence:** If a ray of light strikes the interface of two media at an angle of **0 degrees** (along the normal), the **angle of refraction** is also **0 degrees**. In this specific case, the ray passes through without bending, although its speed still changes.
 
• **Total Internal Reflection (TIR):** This occurs when light travels from a **denser medium** to a **rarer medium** at an angle of incidence greater than the **critical angle**. In this scenario, **Snell’s Law** implies that the sine of the angle of refraction would be greater than **1**, which is mathematically impossible, resulting in the light reflecting back entirely into the denser medium.
 
• **Applications:** Snell’s Law is essential in the design of **optical lenses**, **spectacles**, **microscopes**, **telescopes**, and **fiber optic cables** used in telecommunications.

questions.question: A bus travels a 6 km distance in 20 minutes to go from point A to point B. The bus travels from point B to point A in 30 minutes. What is the average speed in m/s of the bus?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance covered = 6 km + 6 km = 12 km = 12,000 m

Total time taken = 20 min + 30 min = 50 min = 3,000 s

Average speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Average speed = 12,000 ÷ 3,000 = 4 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance from A to B = 6 km

Time from A to B = 20 minutes

Time from B to A = 30 minutes

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

1 km = 1,000 m | 1 minute = 60 seconds

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/812d293c39102f39d72f1daea58527621f68e872ea2ffda505b04cac5c500df9.png] 

⇒ Total Distance = 6 km + 6 km = 12 km

⇒ Total Distance in meters = 12 × 1,000 = 12,000 m

⇒ Total Time = 20 min + 30 min = 50 min

⇒ Total Time in seconds = 50 × 60 = 3,000 s

⇒ Average Speed = 12,000 ÷ 3,000

⇒ Average Speed = 4 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Distances

When an object travels equal distances at speeds x and y, the average speed is given by the harmonic mean: 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Unit Conversion Shortcut

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Uniform Speed vs Average Speed

Uniform speed is constant throughout the journey, whereas average speed is the ratio of total path length to the total time interval taken.</p

questions.question: If the thrust acting on a surface remains constant, how does the pressure change with the area of contact?

options.text: Pressure does not depend on area.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pressure increases when area decreases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pressure** is defined as the **thrust** (force acting perpendicular to a surface) acting per unit **area** of that surface.
 
• The mathematical relationship between these physical quantities is expressed by the formula: **Pressure = Thrust / Area**.
 
• When the **thrust** remains **constant**, pressure is **inversely proportional** to the **area of contact**. This means that if the area increases, the pressure decreases, and if the area decreases, the pressure increases.
 
• Evaluating the given options based on the inverse relationship (**P ∝ 1/A**):
 
 
• Option 1: Pressure decreases when area decreases. ***This statement is incorrect*** because pressure should increase.
 
• Option 2: Pressure increases when area increases. ***This statement is incorrect*** because pressure should decrease.
 
• Option 3: Pressure increases when area decreases. ***This statement is correct*** as it aligns with the inverse proportionality.
 
• Option 4: Pressure does not depend on area. ***This statement is incorrect*** because area is a primary factor in calculating pressure.
 
 
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Pressure increases when area decreases.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Thrust:**
 
 
• It is the **total force** acting **perpendicularly** on a surface.
 
• The **S.I. unit** of thrust is the **Newton (N)**, the same as force.
 
• Thrust is a **vector quantity**, meaning it has both magnitude and direction.
 
 
 
• **Pressure Units:**
 
 
• The **S.I. unit** of pressure is **Newton per square metre (N/m²)**.
 
• In honour of the scientist **Blaise Pascal**, the unit is also called the **Pascal (Pa)**. **1 Pa = 1 N/m²**.
 
• Other common units include the **bar**, **torr**, and **atmosphere (atm)**. **1 atm** is approximately **101,325 Pa**.
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications of Pressure-Area Relationship:**
 
 
• **Sharp Knives:** A sharp knife has a very **small area** at its cutting edge. For the same **thrust** applied by the hand, it produces a **high pressure** that easily cuts through objects.
 
• **School Bags:** These are provided with **broad straps** so that the weight (thrust) of the bag is distributed over a **larger area** of the shoulder, resulting in **less pressure** and more comfort for the student.
 
• **Foundations of Buildings:** High-rise buildings have **wide foundations** to ensure the massive weight is spread over a **large surface area**, preventing the structure from sinking into the ground due to **excessive pressure**.
 
• **Tractors:** Tractors have **broad tires** to reduce the **pressure** on the soft ground of agricultural fields, preventing them from sinking.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• While **force** and **thrust** are **vector quantities**, **pressure** is a **scalar quantity** because it does not have a specific direction associated with it at a point in a fluid or on a surface; it acts in all directions.
 
• In **fluids (liquids and gases)**, pressure increases with **depth** because the weight of the fluid column above (which acts as the thrust) increases as you go deeper.
 
• **Atmospheric Pressure:** The weight of the **Earth's atmosphere** exerts pressure on everything on the surface. At **sea level**, the standard atmospheric pressure is **1.013 x 10⁵ Pa**.

questions.question: Which of the following is INCORRECT about striated muscle?

options.text: Each striated muscle fibre contains a single nucleus
Mostly attached to bones and help in body movement

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Each striated muscle fibre contains a single nucleus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Striated muscles** are primarily those muscles that are under the conscious control of the **somatic nervous system**, which is why they are commonly referred to as **voluntary muscles**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• A defining structural feature of **striated muscle fibers** is that they are **multinucleated**. During development, several **myoblasts** fuse together to form a single muscle fiber, resulting in a **syncytium** where multiple nuclei are present in a single cell, typically located at the periphery. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• These muscles are found extensively throughout the body, particularly in the **limbs** (arms and legs), **body wall**, **face**, and **neck**, where they facilitate complex movements. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• **Striated muscles** are mostly **attached to bones** via **tendons**. Their primary function is to contract and relax to produce **force and motion**, helping in **body movement** and maintaining **posture**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• Microscopically, these muscles appear to have alternating **light and dark bands** (striations) when viewed under a microscope, which is caused by the specific arrangement of **actin and myosin** filaments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Muscles:**
 
 
• **Smooth Muscles:** These are **involuntary muscles** found in the walls of internal organs like the **stomach**, **intestines**, and **blood vessels**. They are **spindle-shaped** and, unlike striated muscles, contain only a **single nucleus** (uninucleated) and lack striations.
 
• **Cardiac Muscles:** Located exclusively in the **heart**, these muscles are **striated** but **involuntary**. They are characterized by **branched fibers** and **intercalated discs** that allow for synchronized contractions. They usually contain **one or two nuclei**.
 
 
 
• **Structural Components:**
 
 
• The functional unit of a striated muscle is the **sarcomere**. It is the segment between two **Z-lines** and contains the machinery required for muscle contraction.
 
• The **Sarcolemma** is the specialized **cell membrane** that surrounds the striated muscle fiber, while the **Sarcoplasm** is the cytoplasm containing high amounts of **glycosomes** and **myoglobin**.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Skeletal Muscle:**
 
 
• Beyond **locomotion**, these muscles play a critical role in **heat production** (thermogenesis) to maintain **body temperature**.
 
• They also serve as a **storage site** for amino acids and glucose (in the form of **glycogen**), which can be utilized by the body during metabolic stress.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Muscle Contraction Mechanism:** The process is explained by the **Sliding Filament Theory**, proposed in **1954**. It states that muscle contraction occurs when **thin filaments** (actin) slide over **thick filaments** (myosin), shortening the **sarcomere** without the filaments themselves changing length.
 
• **Fast-twitch vs. Slow-twitch:** Striated muscles can be categorized into **Type I (slow-twitch)**, which are dense with **capillaries** and **mitochondria** for endurance, and **Type II (fast-twitch)**, which are used for short bursts of **strength or speed**.
 
• **Energy Source:** These muscles utilize **Adenosine Triphosphate (ATP)** as the primary energy source for contraction, which is replenished through **aerobic respiration** or **anaerobic glycolysis** depending on the intensity of the physical activity.

questions.question: లైంగిక కార్యకలాపాల సమయంలో కొన్ని లైంగికంగా సంక్రమించే ఇన్ఫెక్షన్ల (STIలు) వ్యాప్తిని ఎలా తగ్గించవచ్చు?

options.text: సంపర్కం సమయంలో కండోమ్‌ల వంటి రక్షణను ఉపయోగించడం ద్వారా
పగటిపూట మాత్రమే లైంగిక కార్యకలాపాల్లో పాల్గొనడం ద్వారా
ప్రతి లైంగిక చర్యకు ముందు యాంటీబయాటిక్స్ తీసుకోవడం ద్వారా

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**సంపర్కం సమయంలో కండోమ్‌ల వంటి రక్షణను ఉపయోగించడం ద్వారా**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **లైంగికంగా సంక్రమించే ఇన్ఫెక్షన్లు (STIs)**: ఇవి ప్రధానంగా లైంగిక సంపర్కం ద్వారా ఒక వ్యక్తి నుండి మరొకరికి వ్యాపించే బ్యాక్టీరియా, వైరస్‌లు లేదా పరాన్నజీవుల వల్ల కలుగుతాయి.
 
• సంపర్కం సమయంలో **కండోమ్‌లు (Condoms)** వంటి రక్షణ సాధనాలను ఉపయోగించడం వల్ల శారీరక ద్రవాల మార్పిడి అడ్డుకోబడుతుంది. ఇది ఇన్ఫెక్షన్ల వ్యాప్తిని తగ్గించడంలో అత్యంత ప్రభావవంతమైన పద్ధతి. ***అందువల్ల, ఎంపిక 2 సరైనది.***
 
• వ్యక్తులందరితో శారీరక సంబంధాన్ని నివారించడం (Abstinence) అనేది ఇన్ఫెక్షన్ల వ్యాప్తిని పూర్తిగా ఆపగలిగినప్పటికీ, లైంగిక కార్యకలాపాలు నిర్వహించే వ్యక్తుల కోసం ఇది ఆచరణాత్మకమైన నివారణ మార్గం కాదు. ***కాబట్టి, స్టేట్‌మెంట్ 1 ఈ ప్రశ్న సందర్భంలో పరిమితమైనది.***
 
• లైంగిక కార్యకలాపాలు **పగలు** లేదా **రాత్రి** ఏ సమయంలో నిర్వహించినా ఇన్ఫెక్షన్ల వ్యాప్తిపై ఎటువంటి ప్రభావం ఉండదు, ఎందుకంటే వ్యాధికారక క్రిములు కాంతి లేదా సమయంపై ఆధారపడి ఉండవు. ***అందువల్ల, స్టేట్‌మెంట్ 3 తప్పు.***
 
• **యాంటీబయాటిక్స్** కేవలం బ్యాక్టీరియా వల్ల కలిగే ఇన్ఫెక్షన్లకు (ఉదాహరణకు **సిఫిలిస్**) మాత్రమే చికిత్స చేస్తాయి. ముందస్తుగా యాంటీబయాటిక్స్ తీసుకోవడం వల్ల వైరల్ STIల (ఉదాహరణకు **HIV**) నుండి రక్షణ లభించదు మరియు ఇది **యాంటీబయాటిక్ రెసిస్టెన్స్**‌కు దారి తీస్తుంది. ***కాబట్టి, స్టేట్‌మెంట్ 4 తప్పు.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **సాధారణ STIలు**: ప్రపంచవ్యాప్తంగా మరియు భారతదేశంలో అత్యంత సాధారణంగా కనిపించే లైంగిక వ్యాధులలో **HIV/AIDS**, **గోనోరియా (Gonorrhea)**, **సిఫిలిస్ (Syphilis)**, **క్లామిడియా (Chlamydia)** మరియు **హెపటైటిస్ B** ముఖ్యమైనవి.

• **ప్రభుత్వ కార్యక్రమాలు**: భారతదేశంలో **నేషనల్ ఎయిడ్స్ కంట్రోల్ ఆర్గనైజేషన్ (NACO)** ద్వారా **1992** నుండి లైంగిక వ్యాధుల నివారణ మరియు నియంత్రణ కోసం విస్తృతమైన అవగాహన కార్యక్రమాలు నిర్వహించబడుతున్నాయి.

questions.question: If the velocity of a body is doubled, its kinetic energy becomes:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**four times**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kinetic Energy (KE)** is the energy possessed by an object due to its **motion**. It is mathematically expressed by the formula: **KE = 1/2 mv²**, where **m** represents the **mass** of the body and **v** represents its **velocity**.
 
• From the formula, it is evident that the **kinetic energy** of a body is **directly proportional** to the **square of its velocity** (KE ∝ v²), assuming the **mass** remains constant.
 
• If the **velocity** of a body is **doubled** (v becomes 2v), the new kinetic energy (KE') can be calculated as: **KE' = 1/2 m(2v)² = 1/2 m(4v²) = 4 (1/2 mv²)**.
 
• Therefore, when the velocity is increased by a **factor of 2**, the kinetic energy increases by a factor of **2 squared**, which is **4**. Hence, the kinetic energy becomes **four times** its original value.
 
• This relationship highlights that **kinetic energy** is highly sensitive to changes in **speed** compared to changes in **mass**. For instance, if the velocity were tripled, the kinetic energy would become **nine times** the original.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Work-Energy Theorem**: This theorem states that the **net work done** on an object is equal to the **change in its kinetic energy**. If **positive work** is done on a body, its **velocity** increases, leading to a rise in kinetic energy.
 
• **Relationship with Momentum**: Kinetic energy is also related to **linear momentum (p)** by the formula **KE = p² / 2m**. This shows that if the **momentum** of a body is doubled, its kinetic energy also becomes **four times**, provided the **mass** is constant.
 
• **Units and Nature**: The **SI unit** of kinetic energy is the **Joule (J)**, which is equivalent to **1 kg m²/s²**. Kinetic energy is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it has only **magnitude** and no **direction**, and it can never be **negative** because mass is positive and the square of velocity is always non-negative.
 
• **Practical Applications**: This principle is critical in **road safety**. Since **KE ∝ v²**, doubling the speed of a car quadruples the energy involved in a **collision** and significantly increases the **braking distance** required to stop the vehicle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mass vs. Velocity**: While kinetic energy is **linearly proportional** to **mass**, it is **quadratically proportional** to **velocity**. Doubling the **mass** only doubles the kinetic energy, but doubling the **velocity** quadruples it.
 
• **Frame of Reference**: The value of kinetic energy depends on the **observer's frame of reference**. A person sitting in a moving train has **zero kinetic energy** relative to the train but significant kinetic energy relative to an observer standing on the **platform**.
 
• **Types of Kinetic Energy**: Besides **translational kinetic energy** (1/2 mv²), objects can also possess **rotational kinetic energy** (1/2 Iω²) and **vibrational kinetic energy**, depending on their type of motion.
</ul

questions.question: An electric bulb is connected to a 240 { V} generator and draws a current of 0.25 { A} . What is the power consumed by the bulb?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**60 W**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Electric Power** is defined as the rate at which electrical energy is consumed or dissipated in an electric circuit. It represents the work done per unit time.
 
• In this problem, the **Voltage (V)** provided by the generator is **240 V** and the **Current (I)** drawn by the electric bulb is **0.25 A**.
 
• The standard mathematical formula to calculate electric power is **P = V × I**, where **P** is the power, **V** is the potential difference (voltage), and **I** is the current.
 
• Substituting the given **numerical values** into the formula: **Power = 240 × 0.25**.
 
• The calculation yields **60**. Since the **SI unit** of power is the **Watt (W)**, the power consumed by the bulb is **60 W**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 60 W.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ohm's Law and Resistance:**
 
 
• According to **Ohm's Law**, the relationship between voltage, current, and resistance is given by **V = IR**.
 
• If we calculate the resistance of this specific bulb, **R = V / I**, which is **240 / 0.25 = 960 Ohms**. Note that **960** is the **Resistance**, not the power.
 
 
 
• **Alternative Power Formulas:**
 
 
• Power can also be expressed in terms of resistance: **P = I²R** or **P = V² / R**.
 
• Using **P = V² / R** for this bulb: **(240 × 240) / 960 = 57600 / 960 = 60 W**. These formulas are useful when the current or voltage is unknown but resistance is provided.
 
 
 
• **Units of Measurement:**
 
 
• The **Watt** is named after the Scottish inventor **James Watt**. **1 Watt** is equal to **1 Joule per second (1 J/s)**.
 
• Larger units of power include the **Kilowatt (kW)**, where **1 kW = 1,000 Watts**, and the **Horsepower (hp)**, where **1 hp** is approximately **746 Watts**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Distinction between Power and Energy:**
 
 
• **Power (measured in Watts)** is the rate of energy consumption, whereas **Energy (measured in Joules)** is the total amount of work done over a period.
 
• The options **60 J** and **960 J** are incorrect because the **Joule** is a unit of **energy**, not power.
 
 
 
• **Commercial Unit of Electrical Energy:**
 
 
• The commercial unit used for electricity bills is the **Kilowatt-hour (kWh)**, which is often referred to as a "unit."
 
• **1 kWh** is the energy consumed by a **1,000 W** appliance running for **one hour**, which equals **3.6 × 10⁶ Joules**.
 
 
 
• **Practical Application:**
 
 
• Most domestic appliances in **India** operate at a standard voltage of **220 V to 240 V**. The **current** rating helps in determining the appropriate fuse or circuit breaker required for safety **features**.

questions.question: Which of the following reactions is an example of a double displacement reaction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**AgNO3 + NaCl → AgCl + NaNO3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **double displacement reaction** is a type of chemical reaction where **two compounds react**, and the **positive ions (cations)** and the **negative ions (anions)** of the two reactants **switch places**, forming two new compounds.
 
• In the reaction **AgNO3 + NaCl → AgCl + NaNO3**, the **silver ion (Ag+)** from **silver nitrate** combines with the **chloride ion (Cl-)** from **sodium chloride** to form **silver chloride (AgCl)**. Simultaneously, the **sodium ion (Na+)** combines with the **nitrate ion (NO3-)** to form **sodium nitrate (NaNO3)**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• The reaction **CaCO3 → CaO + CO2** involves a single reactant breaking down into two simpler products upon heating. This is classified as a **thermal decomposition reaction**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The reaction **2Mg + O2 → 2MgO** involves two reactants (magnesium and oxygen) combining to form a single product (magnesium oxide). This is known as a **combination reaction** or **synthesis reaction**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The reaction **Zn + H2SO4 → ZnSO4 + H2** involves **Zinc** displacing **Hydrogen** from **sulfuric acid** because zinc is more reactive. This is a **single displacement reaction**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is AgNO3 + NaCl → AgCl + NaNO3.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Precipitation Reactions:** Many **double displacement reactions** result in the formation of an **insoluble solid** that settles out of the solution, known as a **precipitate**. In the given correct option, **AgCl** is a **white precipitate**.
 
• **Neutralization Reactions:** This is another common type of **double displacement reaction** that occurs between an **acid** and a **base** to produce **salt and water**. For example, **HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H2O**.
 
• **Reactivity Series:** While **single displacement** depends heavily on the **reactivity series** (where a more active metal displaces a less active one), **double displacement** usually depends on the **solubility rules** or the formation of a stable product like water or a gas.
 
• **Gas Evolution:** Some double displacement reactions produce a **gas**. For instance, the reaction between **sodium carbonate** and **hydrochloric acid** eventually releases **carbon dioxide (CO2)** gas after an initial ion exchange.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

questions.question: What is the primary component of the plant cell wall?

__
 
• **Cellulose** is the **primary structural component** of the **plant cell wall**, providing the necessary **mechanical strength**, **rigidity**, and **protection** to the plant cell.
 
• Chemically, it is a **polysaccharide** (a complex carbohydrate) consisting of a long, linear chain of **hundreds to thousands** of **glucose units** joined by **beta(1→4) glycosidic bonds**.
 
• It is considered the most **abundant organic polymer** on **Earth**, making up a significant portion of the **biomass** in terrestrial ecosystems.
 
• In the cell wall, cellulose molecules are bundled together to form **microfibrils**, which create a high-tensile **scaffold** that helps the cell withstand **turgor pressure** and maintain its **shape**.
 
• Unlike starch, humans cannot digest cellulose because they lack the enzyme **cellulase**; however, it serves as essential **dietary fiber** in the human diet.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• It is a complex **organic polymer** found primarily in the **secondary cell walls** of **vascular plants**.
 
• **Lignin** provides **structural support**, making the plant **woody** and **rigid**, and plays a crucial role in **water transport** by making cell walls **hydrophobic**. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***

• **Cutin:**
 
 
• **Cutin** is one of the main components of the **plant cuticle**, which covers the **epidermis** of leaves, fruits, and soft stems.
 
• It is a **waxy polymer** that prevents excessive **transpiration** (water loss) and protects the plant from **ultraviolet radiation** and **external stress**. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Hemicellulose and Pectin:**
 
 
• While cellulose provides the framework, **hemicellulose** acts as a **cross-linking agent** between cellulose microfibrils.
 
• **Pectin** is a gel-like **polysaccharide** that fills the spaces between the fibers, providing **flexibility** and helping in **cell-to-cell adhesion** through the **middle lamella**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Composition:** The plant cell wall is typically composed of approximately **35% to 50% cellulose**, **20% to 35% hemicellulose**, and **10% to 25% lignin**.
 
• **Turgor Pressure:** The **rigidity** of the cellulose-based cell wall is vital for maintaining **turgor pressure**, which allows plants to stand upright without a **skeletal system**.
 
• **Discovery:** Cellulose was first discovered and isolated by the **French chemist Anselme Payen** in the **year 1838**.
 
• **Industrial Uses:** Beyond its biological role, cellulose is used extensively in the production of **paper**, **textiles** (like cotton and rayon), and **biofuels**.
</ul

questions.question: When a light ray passes through a rectangular glass slab, the emergent ray is ____________.

options.text: Along the same line as the incident ray
Bent toward the normal without displacement
Parallel to the incident ray but shifted sideward

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parallel to the incident ray but shifted sideward**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a ray of light enters a **rectangular glass slab** from **air**, it undergoes **refraction** twice: once at the air-glass interface and again at the glass-air interface.
 
• At the first surface, light travels from a **rarer medium (air)** to a **denser medium (glass)**, causing the ray to bend **towards the normal**.
 
• At the second surface, light travels from the **denser medium (glass)** back into the **rarer medium (air)**, causing the ray to bend **away from the normal**.
 
• Since the opposite faces of a rectangular glass slab are **parallel** to each other, the extent of bending of the ray of light at the first surface is equal and opposite to the extent of bending at the second surface.
 
• As a result, the **emergent ray** emerges in a direction **parallel** to the **incident ray**. However, there is a **lateral shift** or **sideward displacement** between the original path of the incident ray and the emergent ray. ***Hence, the statement describing it as parallel but shifted sideward is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Refractive Index:** It is a **dimensionless number** that describes how fast light travels through a medium. The refractive index of **glass** is typically around **1.5**, while for **air**, it is approximately **1.0003**.
 
• **Snell's Law:** This law governs refraction and is expressed as **n1 sin(i) = n2 sin(r)**, where **n1** and **n2** are refractive indices of the two media, **i** is the **angle of incidence**, and **r** is the **angle of refraction**.
 
• **Lateral Displacement:** The perpendicular distance between the direction of the **incident ray** and the **emergent ray** is known as **lateral displacement**.
 
• **Factors Affecting Lateral Displacement:**
 
 
• **Thickness of the glass slab:** Lateral displacement is **directly proportional** to the **thickness** of the slab. A thicker slab causes a larger sideward shift.
 
• **Angle of Incidence:** As the **angle of incidence (i)** increases, the lateral displacement also increases.
 
• **Refractive Index:** A higher **refractive index** of the material leads to greater lateral displacement.
 
• **Wavelength of Light:** Lateral displacement depends on the **wavelength** (color) of light. Since **violet light** bends more than **red light**, it experiences more lateral displacement.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• If a light ray falls **normally** (perpendicularly) on the surface of the glass slab, the **angle of incidence is 0 degrees**. In this specific case, the ray passes through without any **deviation** or **lateral displacement**.
 
• The **angle of incidence** is always equal to the **angle of emergence** (i = e) for a rectangular glass slab when the medium on both sides of the slab is the same.
 
• This phenomenon is a practical application of **optics** and is used to demonstrate the **rectilinear propagation of light** and the laws of **refraction** in laboratory experiments.
 
• In **2024**, understanding these principles remains fundamental in fields like **lens design**, **fiber optics**, and **microscopy**.
</ul

questions.question: How does pollination contribute to seed formation in plants?

options.text: By forming a protective seed coat around the ovule

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**By transferring pollen from the anther to the stigma, enabling fertilisation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pollination** is defined as the act of transferring **pollen grains** from the male **anther** of a flower to the female **stigma**. This process is the vital first step in the sexual reproduction of flowering plants.
 
• The primary contribution of pollination to seed formation is that it enables **fertilisation**. Without this transfer, the male gametes contained within the pollen would never reach the female gametes (ovules) located in the **ovary**. ***Hence, option 3 is correct.***
 
• Once a compatible pollen grain lands on the **stigma**, it germinates and produces a **pollen tube**. This tube grows down through the **style** to deliver two male gametes into the **embryo sac** within the **ovule**.
 
• Upon reaching the ovule, one male gamete fuses with the egg cell to form a **zygote**. This fusion is the essence of fertilisation, which eventually triggers the transformation of the **ovule** into a **seed**.
 
• While **nectar** production (Option 4) attracts pollinators, it is a biological "bribe" and not the direct mechanism that forms a seed. Similarly, **seed dispersal** (Option 2) occurs only after the seed is fully formed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Pollination**:
 
 
• **Self-pollination**: Occurs when pollen from the **anther** is deposited on the **stigma** of the same flower or another flower on the same plant. This is common in plants like **peas** and **wheat**.
 
• **Cross-pollination**: The transfer of pollen from the anther of one flower to the stigma of another flower on a different individual of the same species. This promotes **genetic diversity** and is seen in species like **maize** and **sunflowers**.
 
 
 
• **Agents of Pollination**:
 
 
• **Biotic Agents**: These include living organisms such as **bees**, **butterflies**, **birds**, and **bats**. Insects are the most common pollinators, often attracted by **brightly coloured petals** or **scent**.
 
• **Abiotic Agents**: These involve non-living forces such as **wind** (Anemophily) and **water** (Hydrophily). Wind-pollinated plants, like **grasses** and **conifers**, usually produce massive amounts of lightweight pollen.
 
 
 
• **Double Fertilisation**: This is a characteristic feature of **Angiosperms** (flowering plants). One male gamete fuses with the egg to form the **zygote**, while the second male gamete fuses with two **polar nuclei** to form the **triploid endosperm**, which provides nourishment to the developing embryo.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Post-Fertilisation Changes**: After successful pollination and fertilisation, the flower undergoes significant changes. The **sepals**, **petals**, and **stamens** usually wither and fall off.
 
• **Seed and Fruit Development**: The **ovule** develops into the **seed**, which contains the **embryo** (the future plant) and is encased in a protective **seed coat** (Option 1 refers to this post-fertilisation structure). Simultaneously, the **ovary** ripens and develops into the **fruit**.
 
• **Significance**: Pollination is not only essential for the survival of plant species but is also critical for **global food security**. Approximately **75%** of the world’s food crops depend, at least in part, on pollination.
 
• **Economic Value**: Many **agricultural** sectors, including the production of **almonds**, **apples**, and **coffee**, rely heavily on honeybee pollination services to ensure high yields and quality seeds.

questions.question: Which of the following metals is characterised by low density and softness?

__
 
• **Potassium** (chemical symbol **K**, from Neo-Latin kalium) is a chemical element with **Atomic Number 19**. It is a silvery-white metal that is **soft** enough to be easily cut with a **knife** with little force.
 
• It is characterized by an extremely **low density** of approximately **0.862 g/cm³** at **20°C**, which is less than that of **water** (1.0 g/cm³). This physical property causes the metal to **float** on the surface of water while it reacts. ***Hence, the correct answer is Potassium.***
 
• As a member of the **Alkali Metals** (Group 1 of the periodic table), it possesses only **one valence electron** in its outer shell. This single electron is involved in **metallic bonding**, which is relatively weak, leading to the characteristic **softness** and **low melting point** (approx **63.5°C**) of the metal.
 
• Due to its extreme **chemical reactivity**, especially with moisture and air, it is never found as a free element in nature and is typically stored under **mineral oil** or **kerosene** to prevent oxidation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Copper (Cu)**:
 
 
• It is a **transition metal** located in **Group 11** of the periodic table.
 
• Unlike potassium, copper has a high density of approximately **8.96 g/cm³** and is significantly harder. It is known for its excellent **electrical conductivity** and **thermal conductivity**. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Aluminium (Al)**:
 
 
• It is a **post-transition metal** in **Group 13**.
 
• While aluminium is known for being **lightweight** compared to steel (density **2.70 g/cm³**), it is much denser than potassium and is a structural metal, not "soft" in the chemical sense of being cut like wax. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Magnesium (Mg)**:
 
 
• It is an **alkaline earth metal** found in **Group 2** of the periodic table with **Atomic Number 12**.
 
• Its density is approximately **1.74 g/cm³**. While it is the lightest structural metal, it is harder than alkali metals like potassium and sodium because it has **two valence electrons**, strengthening its metallic lattice. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***

• **Density Comparisons**: Only three metals in the periodic table are light enough to float on water: **Lithium** (lightest solid element), **Sodium**, and **Potassium**.

questions.question: The value of (1 - (1)/(2))(1 - (1)/(3))(1 - (1)/(4))(1 - (1)/(5)) dots dots dots (1 - (1)/(m)) is equal to:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For product series like (1 − 1/n), simplify the first 2-3 terms to identify the continuous cancellation pattern.

(1 − 1/2) × (1 − 1/3) × (1 − 1/4) ... = (1/2) × (2/3) × (3/4) ...

The numerator of each term exactly cancels the denominator of the previous term.

Remaining value = (Numerator of first term) ÷ (Denominator of last term) = 1 / m.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = (1 − 1/2)(1 − 1/3)(1 − 1/4)(1 − 1/5) ... (1 − 1/m)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Simplifying each bracket individually by taking the LCM.

⇒ Expression = [(2 − 1) / 2] × [(3 − 1) / 3] × [(4 − 1) / 4] × [(5 − 1) / 5] ... [(m − 1) / m]

⇒ Expression = (1/2) × (2/3) × (3/4) × (4/5) ... ((m − 1) / m)

⇒ Here, the denominator of each term gets continuously canceled by the numerator of the consecutive fraction.

⇒ Specifically, 2 cancels with 2, 3 with 3, 4 with 4, all the way up to (m − 1).

⇒ After complete cancellation across the entire series, only the numerator of the very first fraction and the denominator of the final fraction remain.

⇒ Result = 1 / m

**∴ The correct answer is 1/m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Telescoping Series

A series where intermediate terms cancel each other out, leaving only the initial and final terms. It frequently appears in fraction products and difference summations.

Addition Series Pattern

(1 + 1/2)(1 + 1/3)(1 + 1/4) ... (1 + 1/n) = (3/2) × (4/3) × (5/4) ... ((n+1)/n) = (n + 1) / 2.

Difference of Squares Series

(1 − 1/2²)(1 − 1/3²)(1 − 1/4²) ... (1 − 1/n²) = (n + 1) / 2n.

questions.question: If P is a prime number, what is the HCF of P and P + 1 ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Any two consecutive integers are always co-prime to each other.

Since P and P + 1 are consecutive numbers, they share no common factors other than 1.

The condition that P is a prime number is extra information, as the HCF of any two consecutive numbers is always 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First number = P (where P is a prime number)

Second number = P + 1

**Concept Used:**

If a number 'd' divides two numbers 'a' and 'b', then 'd' must also divide their difference (a − b).

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of P and P + 1 be x.

⇒ This implies that x completely divides both P and P + 1.

⇒ By the property of divisibility, x must also divide the difference between the two numbers.

⇒ Difference = (P + 1) − P = 1

⇒ So, x must divide 1 completely.

⇒ The only positive integer that can divide 1 is 1.

⇒ Hence, x = 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are defined as co-prime (or mutually prime) if their Highest Common Factor (HCF) is exactly 1. All consecutive integers fall into this category.

LCM of Co-prime Numbers

The Least Common Multiple (LCM) of any two co-prime numbers is simply the product of the two numbers. For example, the LCM of P and P + 1 is P × (P + 1) = P² + P.

Divisibility Rule of Difference

If an integer divides two numbers A and B (where A > B), it will also divide their difference A − B, as well as their sum A + B. This concept is the foundational basis of the Euclidean algorithm for finding HCF.
</p
